blocks.text: When the psalm praises the “law of Jehovah,” it speaks of torah: the covenant instruction given through Moses, describing how God’s redeemed people are to live before him. Ancient legal and treaty traditions provide a broad background, but torah is not presented here as merely one generic legal code. This context clarifies why the psalm describes it not only as authoritative but also as restorative, wise, joyful, illuminating, and more desirable than gold or honey.
